lit.'<p>La <b>biotecnología</b> aprovecha mi:
'

Biotechnology puts microorganisms to work: yeast ferments glucose into ethanol and CO₂ (the CO₂ makes bread rise; the ethanol, wine); lactic bacteria turn lactose into lactic acid (yoghurt, cheeses); fungi and bacteria produce antibiotics and insulin. In Chile, biomining uses bacteria such as Acidithiobacillus to release copper from ores.

'
lit.'<p>Los <b>antibióticos</b> matan bacter:
'

Antibiotics kill bacteria or stop them growing. A population contains, by chance, a few resistant bacteria (orange). When the antibiotic is applied, the sensitive ones die and the resistant ones multiply: the culture becomes resistant. That is why antibiotics should be used only on prescription, the course completed, and never against viruses.

'
lit.'<p>Los <b>hongos</b> son eucariotas que:
'

Fungi are eukaryotes that feed by absorbing organic matter: they are major decomposers. Yeasts are single-celled and reproduce by budding (a daughter cell sprouts). Moulds form filaments called hyphae. Some cause disease (athlete’s foot); others make foods and medicines, such as penicillin.

'
lit.'<p>Los <b>microorganismos</b> solo se v:
'

Microorganisms can only be seen with a microscope. Bacteria (≈ 1–5 μm) are prokaryotic cells, with no nucleus. Microscopic fungi, such as yeasts (≈ 5–10 μm), are eukaryotic cells. Viruses (≈ 0.02–0.3 μm) are not cells: they are genetic material inside a protein coat. Here they are enlarged at different scales.

'
lit.'<p>Un <b>virus</b> no come ni crece ni:
'

A virus does not feed, grow or reproduce on its own: it is an obligate parasite. It binds to a cell, injects its genetic material and forces the cell to build new viruses, which burst out and destroy it (the lytic cycle). Viruses cause diseases such as flu, measles or COVID-19. Antibiotics do not work against them; vaccines and some antivirals do.

'
lit.'<p>Una bacteria tiene <b>pared celular<:
'

A bacterium has a cell wall, membrane, cytoplasm with ribosomes, a circular chromosome (nucleoid), sometimes plasmids and flagella. It reproduces by binary fission: at 37 °C, some double every 20–30 min. A culture shows a lag phase, an exponential phase, a stationary phase (nutrients run out) and a death phase. Temperature changes how fast they grow.

'
